correctness.rationale: Reconstructed conditional second-moment evolution M=diag((1-eta)^2,(1-6eta)^2)P for symmetric two-state chain. Stability from either deterministic starting mode is rho(M)<1, including reducible p=1 and periodic p=0 cases. Direct symbolic expansion verifies det(I-M)=eta C_p(eta) and cubic discriminant -144(2p-1)G(p) with G=23675p^3-38914p^2+803p+36. Unique p* in (0,1/2) has value 0.04318988247 and forms a double larger-root boundary; at p=0, C0=-36(eta-1/2)(eta-2/3)(eta-7/6) yielding two stable intervals. Above p* one interval; for p>=1/2, PSD P and matrix-convex symmetric representative give connected strict sublevel set; endpoints 14/37 at p=1/2, 1/3 at p=1. Independent exact symbolic discriminant, factorization, and rational p=1/50 eta=3/5 unstable versus eta=9/10 stable verified.

originality.rationale: Published Markov jump linear systems provide the general necessity and sufficiency of lifted spectral-radius mean-square stability, which the source explicitly credits. The specialized disconnected learning-rate set, its algebraic persistence threshold p* and root-coalescence topology for curvatures 1 and 6 are not stated in the inspected broad full primary Ling–Deng and Lee–Halder–Bhattacharya papers. A potentially overlapping 2000 scalar-jump source has only abstract available, retained as a risk rather than declared noncovering.
residual_risks: Gray, González and Patilkulkarni (2000) conference text could not be accessed in full, so an equivalent reentrant scalar-jump example cannot be excluded.
Only curvature pair (1,6), symmetric switching and pure multiplicative scalar gradient model are classified.

value.rationale: An explicitly strongly convex two-sample optimization instance displays nonmonotone, reentrant admissible learning-rate windows, and the exact transition identifies the parameter where this instability topology disappears. This is a motivated sharp boundary phenomenon not merely a restatement of the classical rho<1 criterion.
